## The command (run it in a real terminal, during a live call)

```bash
pid=$(pgrep -f 'livekit-server --config' | head -1); echo "pid=${pid:-NONE}"
for f in udp udp6; do
  awk 'NR>1{split($2,a,":"); p=strtonum("0x" a[2]);
      if (p>=50000 && p<=50100) {
        ip=sprintf("%d.%d.%d.%d",
          strtonum("0x" substr(a[1],7,2)), strtonum("0x" substr(a[1],5,2)),
          strtonum("0x" substr(a[1],3,2)), strtonum("0x" substr(a[1],1,2)))
        print ip":"p }}' /proc/$pid/net/$f
done | sort -u
```

`/proc/<pid>/net/udp`, not `ss` — but read the two caveats below before you trust either.

**Caveat 1 — from *my* Bash this probe can only ever return a lie.** My tool calls execute under `bwrap --unshare-all --tmpfs /tmp`, i.e. a private network namespace with only `lo`, and with `/tmp` masked.
